memo.verdict: Progress to Early-Stage Assessment. Direction neutral, conviction medium. Not a park. The Triaging stage test asks whether the case carries large amounts of positive change forces, and it plainly does: guidance rose twice inside one financial year, from low single-digit to mid-teens underlying operating profit growth, and consensus financial year 2026 operating profit moved from £180-185m to £205-208m. The memo declines to park on valuation because Element E3 (Sufficient total-shareholder-return / valuation upside) is not in scope at Triaging, so parking on price would pre-empt the stage that owns valuation. Two named conditions attach. First, Early-Stage Assessment must resolve the financial year 2027 comparative created by the memory-shortage pull-forward unwind. Second, Element E3 must be struck against a live, non-stale forward multiple, because the master-dashboard valuation file for SCT-GB is flagged stale and its 16.8x forward price-to-earnings will not reconcile with the 2,052p live price. Timing: Early-Stage Assessment should follow the financial year 2026 preliminary results expected October 2026. The memo's own one-line framing: a genuine top-decile quality compounder whose change forces are intact and whose entry point has closed over roughly six months.
case: The change forces are dense on both axes, which is the Triaging test. Externally, artificial-intelligence infrastructure demand is broad-based and expands the addressable market rather than substituting within it. Enterprise adoption requires upgrades to power, compute, network bandwidth and cybersecurity before applications run. Management reports double-digit growth across all five technology towers simultaneously, not a mix shift between them. Over 95% of United Kingdom enterprise hardware expenditure transacts through established channel partners. Hardware gross invoiced income rose 78.7% in the first half on enterprise compute and networking upgrades. United Kingdom computer programming and consultancy output rose 3.7% quarter on quarter after 3.8%, decoupling technology demand from weak headline growth.

Internally, four distinct changes are live at once, unusual for a business with a twenty-year unchanged model: the first-ever acquisition (Oakland Group Services, April 2025, £8.0m upfront cash plus earnouts, £9.4m total fair value, 70 specialist data and artificial-intelligence consultants, with a £1.2m fair-value increase in contingent consideration booked as leads exceeded underwriting); the Dynamics 365 sales and human-resources platform rebuild carrying £20m to £25m of multi-year charges; the CatNav proprietary assistant automating account-manager workflow, rebate tracking and bid matching; and an ambition reset lifting the wallet-share target from 20-25% toward 50-60%.

Delivery congruency is the best-evidenced fact in the memo and grades A. Twenty consecutive years of double-digit gross profit growth to £494.3m in financial year 2025, spanning the global financial crisis and the pandemic. Softcat posted 27.3% underlying operating profit growth in the first half, outpacing every European reseller peer.
counter_case: The Risks report's own stage recommendation, quoted in the memo. Its §14 Stage Progression states the investigation "warrants a HOLD with conditional progression stance rather than an immediate pass or full progression decision", and that the investment "should progress to limited position sizing at 50-75% of target weight pending closure of these data gaps". The memo ADOPTS this rather than overriding it, on the ground that conditional progression and progress-to-Early-Stage-Assessment are the same decision expressed in two vocabularies. It goes further in one respect: the Risks report's downside language, describing 870p as "substantial downside from current trading levels", was struck against a materially lower share price, so entry-point risk today is worse than that report records.

The FALSE FRIEND profile wins the competing-hypotheses matrix. It carries only two minor inconsistencies against five hard inconsistencies for the bull YES profile and four for the bear NO profile. The memo accepts this finding and carries it as Element E8 RA8 at D. At least six independent markers fire simultaneously: gross invoiced income grew 33.3% while gross profit grew only 22.6%, a gap of over ten percentage points; underlying cash conversion of 147.6% was inflated by a £42.4m advance payment from a single customer, normalising to 102.4% against a historical target range of 85-95%; management attributes roughly 40% of first-half operating profit growth to pull-forwards and lumpy deals; wage costs grew 15.4% against 10.5% headcount growth, so operating leverage is being consumed by pay; group take-rate fell from 14.6% to 13.7% to 13.4% across three consecutive periods; and Jefferies estimates pull-forwards contributed £7m to £10m of first-half gross profit that will not repeat. The single disconfirming datum the Risks report itself records is that customer numbers still grew 3.5%.
triggers: Six key questions for Early-Stage Assessment. How large is the financial year 2027 comparative headwind once memory-shortage pull-forwards unwind. What is the true organic growth rate excluding lumpy large solutions projects, which Jefferies puts closer to high single digits. What is the financial year 2027 impact of Microsoft partner incentive changes on consolidated gross margin, which the company has not quantified. What are the standalone operating margins of the expanding professional services division, which remain undisclosed. What is the public versus private sector margin split, which management has not published transparently. Where does the forward multiple actually sit, once a non-stale valuation extract is available.

Five monitoring triggers. Wage inflation persistently exceeding gross profit growth for three consecutive quarters would confirm the margin failure mode. Gross invoiced income expanding more than 500 basis points faster than gross profit for two consecutive quarters signals adverse mix. Gross profit per customer falling below £50k, or gross profit per employee below £195k, would invalidate the productivity thesis. Sequential declines in back-end vendor rebates per pound of software invoiced over two periods would confirm vendor disintermediation. A public Microsoft announcement cutting United Kingdom partner transaction incentives by more than twenty percent would force a full re-run.
What would make the view bullish. A financial year 2026 result showing organic growth excluding large deals above 10%, with take-rate stabilising.
What would make the view bearish. A first-half financial year 2027 print showing gross profit growth below 10%, which Deutsche Bank already models at 7.5% for the second half.
The single most useful next datapoint. Gross profit per customer and per employee in the fourth quarter, which separate durable productivity from pull-forward.

If parking were chosen instead. Reassessment criteria would be a share price back inside the consensus target range plus a clean post-pull-forward comparative, with Softcat on the quality-compounder watchlist monitored semi-annually at results.
